key_insight: Deposition-only charge-shift strings remove the per-bit capacitor, transistor, tungsten contact and EUV; one sense node per 64 bits is a real resource-intensity lever for block-access memory.
killer_doubt: Bit 64 needs 192 transfers: at imec's CTE 0.98 only ~2% survives; >=0.9995 needed. At ~6 MHz a read takes ~10 us; 60 nm pitch is ~2.5x tighter than NAND.
decisive_experiment: 32-64-tier vertical IGZO CCD pillars (university fab or imec IIAP): measure CTE per transfer vs clock (1-50 MHz) and temperature, and end-to-end packet loss after 192 transfers. ~$600k.
prior_art: imec IGZO CCD: planar 142-bit (IEDM 2024, CTE>98%), vertical 3D CCD (IMW 2026) for CXL buffer (via search snippet, prior logs). Merge into I-10793/N-08.

key_insight: Frozen weights need no writes, so endurance and refresh vanish. Maskless via writing removes the per-model mask set that limits hardwired-model chips.
killer_doubt: Multi-beam writers need ~10 h per mask plate; a 300 mm wafer is ~5x that area, so 4-8 via layers is ~200+ tool-hours per wafer. Diode-less via crosspoints short rows.
decisive_experiment: E-beam write a 1 Mb via crosspoint with resistive via fill on a university tool. Measure read margin vs array size, plus write time per cm2, then feed a per-model cost model against HBM. ~$150k.
prior_art: Taalas HC1 mask-ROM weights, AMD acquiring (via search snippet, prior logs); Matrix Semiconductor 3D OTP; eASIC via-configurable ASICs; Multibeam direct-write e-beam [training knowledge].

key_insight: Same mechanism as I-02068, using masks. Size-coded 2-bit vias on a mature node reach near-1b-DRAM density with zero refresh, and only the via mask is re-spun per model.
killer_doubt: Taalas already hardwires weights with ~2 masks per model. Each update costs masks and an ~8-12 week fab turn while models change every ~3-6 months; 4-level vias face CD spread.
decisive_experiment: Tape out a size-coded 2-bit via array on a mature-node MPW (130/65 nm). Measure 4-level resistance distributions and read margin over ~1e6 vias, plus margin across temperature. ~$100k.
prior_art: Taalas HC1 mask-ROM weights (AMD acquiring, via search snippet, prior logs); NOR/NAND mask ROM; multi-level implant-coded mask ROM (1990s) [training knowledge]. Dup of I-02068.

key_insight: Dense decode re-activates every weight row each token, so activations already restore it. Per-region activation timestamps could retire blanket REF and its tRFC blackout for streamed HBM regions.
killer_doubt: MoE decode touches ~5-10% of experts per token, so many weight rows go unread for >32 ms. Dense-model upside is 5-15% bandwidth; retention rejects are a few percent of dies.
decisive_experiment: Ramulator 2 with real dense and MoE LLM decode traces: histogram row-activation intervals against the 32 ms window and count rows needing targeted refresh. Software only, ~$50k.
prior_art: Smart Refresh (Ghosh and Lee, MICRO 2007) skips recently activated rows; RANA data-lifetime eDRAM refresh (ISCA 2018); prior batch I-04810 dropped on the same mechanism.

key_insight: Positive-feedback neutralisation cuts the effective load of an unchanged 512-cell bitline ~3x, so a ~1.1 fF (~260 nm) capacitor suffices. That is small enough for a 3D-tier capacitor.
killer_doubt: Noise and residual offset scale 3.3x at Cn/Cbl=0.7: 3 mV after auto-zero becomes ~10 mV of a 50 mV budget. Needs ~8k >=1 GHz amplifiers at 2F pitch per activation.
decisive_experiment: 28-65 nm MPW: 512-cell emulated bitlines with 1-5 fF MOM cells, each with a per-bitline neutraliser and auto-zero. Measure gain spread, stability across mats at Cn/Cbl 0.5-0.8, energy, and error rate vs Cs. ~$400k.
prior_art: SRAM negative-capacitance bitlines (Mostafa et al., IEEE TVLSI); US 8872938 NC sense amp (via search snippet); electrophysiology headstage neutralisation. No DRAM version found.

key_insight: Compressing before self-refresh lets PASR switch off the vacated segments. On phones, idle DRAM power directly sets standby life.
killer_doubt: Only idle refresh power improves (~0.49 W per 64 GB RDIMM), with no cost/bit or capacity gain. Linux zram plus LPDDR PASR already captures much of it; ~16 s break-even.
decisive_experiment: On an LPDDR5 phone dev board, script zram compaction and PASR masks at idle. Measure standby DRAM power and wake latency over 1-week user traces. ~$50k.
prior_art: LPDDR partial-array self-refresh; Linux zram/zswap and compaction; RAMZzz rank power-down via page migration (SC 2012) [training knowledge]; GreenDIMM sub-array power-down.

key_insight: Compression slack can pay for strong ECC inside the same 64 B slot, which zeroes the capacity cost of ECC-relaxed refresh or margin for compressible data.
killer_doubt: BF16 lines compress to ~44 B, but FP8/FP4 weights and KV carry ~6.5-7 bits/byte, leaving under the 10 B needed. One incompressible line pins its 8 KB row fast.
decisive_experiment: Measure per-line compressibility (<=54 B) of real BF16, FP8 and FP4 weights, KV and activations from vLLM runs, and the share of fully compressible 8 KB rows. Software, ~$30k.
prior_art: COP compress-and-protect main memory (Palframan, Kim, Lipasti, ISCA 2015); Hi-ECC refresh relaxation (Wilkerson et al., ISCA 2010); RAIDR retention binning (ISCA 2012).

key_insight: Capacity memory need not share the GPU's 85-95 C. A 35 C sled buys 4-18x retention, which can be spent on refresh, multi-level margin or shorter capacitors.
killer_doubt: Tail cells are GIDL or trap-assisted (Ea ~0.2-0.3 eV), which caps the gain at ~3-5x. Refresh is 16-33% of idle DRAM power, so the system gain is ~10-20%.
decisive_experiment: DRAM Bender sweep of DDR5/LPDDR5 tail-cell retention at 35-95 C on ~20 dies to extract tail Ea. ~$60k; partial data already exist (Liu et al., ISCA 2013).
prior_art: Liu et al. ISCA 2013 retention vs temperature; JEDEC 2x refresh above 85 C; temperature-compensated self-refresh; liquid-cooled DIMMs; prior batch I-07481 dropped.

key_insight: The arithmetic holds: t=2 BCH over 144 b at p=1e-4 leaves ~60 failing words per 16 Gb die, so random single-cell defects cost only ~6% in check bits.
killer_doubt: Patterning defects cluster (a bitline bridge kills 512-1,024 cells) and redundancy already handles them. Hard faults at 1e-4 consume VRT/soft-error margin; overlay, not defects, blocks cheap patterning.
decisive_experiment: Map failing-bit spatial classes (single, line, cluster) on ~100 reject DDR5/LPDDR5 dies with DRAM Bender. Then model ECC-plus-sparing yield under NIL and DSA defect signatures. ~$80k.
prior_art: Row and column redundancy (decades); DDR5 on-die SEC ECC adopted for scaling yield; ArchShield (ISCA 2013); NAND bad-block management.

key_insight: Static SA offset lets row-wise codewords spread each SA's errors. A t=8 BCH at raw BER 1e-4 halves capacitor height (AR 62 to 30); 3D tiers need only ~0.6 fF.
killer_doubt: Non-iid errors (VRT, pattern coupling, SA-offset drift) may burst past t=8 per 512 b. Check bits add 9-21 points of area against a 2x shorter pillar; ~8,800-electron cells are softer.
decisive_experiment: DRAM Bender/FPGA on 20-50 DDR5 dies: emulate half signal with a cut tRAS restore and lowered VPP, then log error positions per 512 b codeword across 1e12+ reads and 45-95 C. Fit burst tails against t=8. ~$150k.
prior_art: DDR5 on-die ECC and the LPDDR6/HBM4 ECC trend; Hi-ECC (ISCA 2010); NAND LDPC soft sensing; ECC(552,512) gain-cell refresh study (arXiv 2607.16042, via prior snippet).

key_insight: Weights are written once and read 1e5-3e6 times a day, so HBF wears by read disturb, not P/E cycles. Interleaving tensors and alternating replicas spread the disturb budget.
killer_doubt: SSD firmware has run per-block read counters and read reclaim for 15+ years; the SanDisk/SK hynix HBF controller will include them, leaving no defensible invention.
decisive_experiment: Replay LLM decode read traces on raw pSLC/TLC NAND with a tester. Measure RBER growth vs reads per block, and relocation write amplification with and without replicas. ~$100k.
prior_art: SanDisk/SK hynix High Bandwidth Flash (2025-26); SSD FTL read-disturb management (read counters, read reclaim); stage-2 R32 cites HBF for weight streaming.

key_insight: BEOL wiring routed around folds replaces TSVs, micro-bumps and die alignment. ~20,000 wires cross a 10 mm fold edge, above HBM TSV counts, from one planar wafer flow.
killer_doubt: No known-good-die sort: 8 dies at 90% yield give 0.9^8 = 43% good stacks. 16 polymer interfaces give ~8 K/W, too hot above ~3 W; HBM tax is mainly die-area.
decisive_experiment: Fold a 2-3 um polyimide/Cu membrane carrying 8 die images, with <=1 um-pitch daisy chains through 33 um-radius hinges. Measure resistance and opens after 1,000 cycles at -40/125 C, plus spare-die bypass. ~$300k.
prior_art: EU ORIGENAL foil-TFT folding (3-layer interconnected stack) and 2000s folded-flex 3D packages (via search snippet); Illinois Si-nanomembrane stacking. No folded memory membrane found.
